title: France's household goods consumption falls 0.5% in August
summary:
France household goods consumption fell 0.5 per cent month on month in August 2026, after a revised 0.4 per cent rise in July. 
Textile-clothing spending still increased 0.3 per cent, though slower than July’s 0.6 per cent gain. 
Energy weakness drove the decline, while engineered goods and durable goods continued to rise.

title: What drove India's manufacturing PMI to a 7-month high in September?
summary:
India’s manufacturing PMI rose to 55.1 in September from 52.8 in August, marking a seven-month high.
Stronger domestic and export demand, including for textiles, boosted new orders and output, while hiring and inventory accumulation resumed. 
Business confidence reached a four-month high, although input and selling price pressures also increased.

title: South Africa’s textile & apparel imports down 5.5% in Jan-Aug
summary:

Exports stayed almost steady at 15,820.1 million rand, against 15,788.4 million rand a year earlier.
August imports eased 11.1 per cent month on month and exports eased 12.6 per cent; export capacity remains constrained by logistics, energy and limited value-added manufacturing.

title: Netherlands' economy shows modest improvement in September: CBS
summary:
The Netherlands’ business-cycle reading improved in September, but 9 of 13 indicators stayed below long-term trends.
July goods exports rose 2.1 per cent year on year, with higher machinery shipments relevant to trade flows.
Manufacturing output jumped 9.0 per cent in July, while bankruptcies, vacancies and unemployment remain demand-risk signals for sourcing teams.

title: India’s growth resilience faces energy & capital flow pressures: S&P
summary:
India needs to revive private investment, strengthen infrastructure and address energy and financial bottlenecks to sustain growth, according to S&P Global and Crisil. 
Their report estimated that achieving developed-economy status by 2047 required annual GDP growth of roughly 7.8 per cent. 
Despite strong economic buffers, higher oil prices and rainfall shortfalls posed challenges to growth.

title: Austria nears full $4.5 bn recovery fund disbursement after EU review
summary:
Austria’s fifth and final RRF payment request for €306 million (~$348 million) has received a positive European Commission assessment.
The request would lift Austria’s RRF payouts to €3.96 billion (~$4.5 billion), covering 100 per cent of its plan once cleared.
Measures include industrial decarbonisation, rail freight shift, broadband expansion and research funding relevant to supply chains.

title: Vietnam’s textile sector faces a new growth test?
summary:
Vietnam’s textile and garment exports reached an estimated $33.02 billion in the first eight months of 2026, up 6.7 per cent year on year.
Textiles and yarn rose 37.4 per cent, while apparel exports increased 1.6 per cent, reports citing Vinatex said.
Manufacturers face smaller orders, shorter lead times, input-cost volatility, import dependence and rules-of-origin pressure.

title: Germany's import prices rise 8.3% in August 2026
summary:
Germany’s import prices rose 8.3 per cent year on year in August 2026, the steepest increase since December 2022, while export prices climbed 4.7 per cent, Destatis reported. 
Energy and intermediate goods drove import inflation, reflecting the Middle East war’s impact. 
Monthly import and export prices increased 1.0 and 0.4 per cent, respectively. Imported consumer goods became cheaper year on year.

title: Germany's employment falls 0.1% in August 2026
summary:
Germany had around 45.41 million residents in employment in August 2026, down 0.1 per cent month on month after seasonal adjustment.
The unadjusted count fell 0.2 per cent from July and 0.5 per cent from August 2025, extending the year-on-year decline since January 2025.
For apparel and textile employers, the data point to a softer labour market backdrop in Germany.

title: UAE, Egypt renew $1.36 bn currency swap for five years
summary:

The arrangement is aimed at supporting bilateral trade, investment and local-currency settlements between the two markets.
For exporters, importers and sourcing teams, it signals continued official backing for cross-border payment channels.
